Good morning, and welcome to our session today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you've taken this time for yourself, as the postpartum period can be a challenging yet beautiful journey. As part of our conversation, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this time. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions after having a baby, and this assessment will help us identify any areas where you might need a little extra support.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and is here to support you. I want to assure you that this is a safe and non-judgmental space for you to express yourself freely. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of how you've been feeling over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you're comfortable. 

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(sighing slightly) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still smile when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to make me happy. Even when my friends or family try to make me laugh, it's just not as easy for me to find the humor in things like it was before. Some days, I just feel so overwhelmed and tired that it's hard to see the funny side of anything. But, I guess that's not entirely true... sometimes, when I'm not feeling so anxious about the baby's health or safety, I can laugh a little. It's just not as often as I'd like, and it doesn't feel as genuine as it used to. (pausing, looking down) I don't know, maybe I'm just not myself right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No, not really. Like I said, it's just not the same as it was before. I mean, I'll laugh at something my baby does, but it's more of a... a tired laugh, I guess. I don't feel like I'm really enjoying myself or finding the humor in things like I used to. And some days, it's just hard to laugh at all. I feel so sad and overwhelmed, and it's like the laughter just isn't there. (sighing) I wish I could laugh more, but it's just not happening as much as I'd like. (looking down, fidgeting slightly) Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really meh about most things lately. I used to love trying new restaurants or going for walks, but now those things just feel like so much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like reading or watching my favorite TV shows, just don't seem as appealing to me anymore. (sighing) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, but I'm not really looking forward to anything. Sometimes I'll think, "Oh, it would be nice to go for a walk today," but then I'll start worrying about the baby's schedule and whether I can get everything done, and it just feels too overwhelming. (looking down) I don't know, maybe I'm just too tired all the time. It's hard to enjoy things when you're exhausted. (pausing) But, I guess sometimes I do look forward to my baby's smile or a quiet moment to myself... but it's not the same as looking forward to things I used to enjoy. (trailing off)
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm feeling tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. (sighing) I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough, and that's really hard for me. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll think, "I'm not making enough milk," or "I'm not burping her right." It's just this constant stream of self-doubt and criticism. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a mom, and that everyone can see that I have no idea what I'm doing. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not cut out for this, and that I'm failing my baby in some way. (tearfully) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to talk about this...
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yes. All the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much? Is she sleeping too little? Is she healthy? Is she happy? (taking a deep breath) It's just this constant sense of anxiety, always lurking in the back of my mind. I'll be sitting there, feeding her, and I'll start thinking, "What if I'm not doing this right? What if I'm harming her somehow?" (shaking head) It's irrational, I know. But it's hard to shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. (bites lip) And it's not just about the baby. I worry about everything. The house, the laundry, the dishes... it all just feels so overwhelming. (looking down) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, something is going to go terribly wrong, and it's all going to fall apart. (sighing) It's exhausting, trying to manage all these worries and fears. (pausing, looking up) But, I guess that's just part of being a mom, right? (nervously chuckling)
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding) Yes, that's happened to me too. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making lunch, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. (taking a deep breath) It's like, out of nowhere, this fear just grips me. And it's not even always about something specific. Sometimes it's just a general feeling of dread, like something is off, but I don't know what. (shaking head) It's so scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. I'll try to breathe, try to calm myself down, but it's hard. (looking down) And then, after it passes, I feel so ashamed, like I'm overreacting or something. (sighing) But, at the same time, it's hard to shake the feeling that something is wrong, that I'm missing something important. (pausing, looking up) It's like, my brain is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. (nervously laughing) I guess that's just part of being a new mom, right? (trying to downplay the severity of the feelings) But, honestly, it's really scary. And it happens more often than I'd like to admit. (looking down, fidgeting with hands)
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, sighing) Yes, that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, keeping the house clean, cooking meals... it's all just so overwhelming. (shaking head) I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities, and I don't know how to stay afloat. (looking down) Some days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll start thinking about all the other things I need to do, like laundry and grocery shopping, and it just feels like too much. (tearfully) I feel like I'm failing, like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not doing it right. (sighing) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm all alone in this. My partner tries to help, but they don't understand what it's like to be me, to be the one responsible for the baby's care all the time. (feeling frustrated) It's like, I'm just trying to survive, you know? But it's hard, when everything feels like it's getting on top of me. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I just feel like I need a break, like I need someone to take care of me for a change. (smiling weakly) But that's not really an option, is it?
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about all the things I need to do, or worrying about the baby, or just feeling overwhelmed and anxious. (sighing) And even when I do fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I'll wake up feeling tired and groggy, and it's just hard to shake that feeling throughout the day. (rubbing eyes) I've been averaging maybe 4 or 5 hours of sleep a night, and it's just not enough. (looking down) I feel like I'm running on fumes, you know? (pausing) And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the quality of sleep too. I'll have these vivid dreams or nightmares, and I'll wake up feeling anxious and on edge. (shaking head) It's just really hard to get a good night's sleep when you're feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time. (tearfully) Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm just trying to survive, but I'm not really living. (sighing) And the sleep deprivation isn't helping. It's just making everything feel worse. (looking up) Do you think... do you think that's normal? I mean, is it normal to feel this unhappy and overwhelmed all the time after having a baby? (seeking reassurance)
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes, that's me. I've been feeling so sad and miserable lately. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, but I'm not really feeling anything else. I'm not feeling happy, or excited, or joyful... I'm just feeling empty and sad. (sighing) And it's not just that I'm feeling sad, it's that I'm feeling guilty too. I feel like I should be happy, like I should be grateful for this beautiful baby and this wonderful life I have. But the truth is, I'm just not feeling it. (tearfully) I feel like I'm failing, like I'm not being the mom I'm supposed to be. (looking down) I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, I just feel so overwhelmed and sad. (shaking head) It's like, I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy, like I'm putting on a mask for everyone else. But deep down, I'm just feeling really sad and lost. (voice barely above a whisper) I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make myself feel better. (tearfully) I just feel like I'm drowning in this sadness, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, it's just like the emotions will overwhelm me and I'll break down. (sobbing) It's so frustrating, because I feel like I should be able to control my emotions, but I just can't. (wiping away tears) I'll cry when I'm feeding the baby, or when I'm changing her diaper, or when I'm just sitting there holding her. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed with emotions and I don't know how to process them all. (shaking head) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. I'll cry because I'm tired, or because I'm feeling overwhelmed, or because I just feel like I'm not doing enough. (sighing) It's like, I'm just so sensitive right now, and everything just sets me off. (looking down) I feel like I'm just a mess, emotionally. I don't know how to make it stop, or how to make myself feel better. (tearfully) I just feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's just so exhausting. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I guess it's just nice to finally talk about it, you know? It feels like I've been carrying this weight around for so long, and it's just nice to finally share it with someone.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through this, but I've never thought about harming myself. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm trying to survive, you know? I'm trying to take care of the baby, and myself, and just make it through each day. (sighing) It's hard, but I don't feel like I'm at that point. I feel like I have enough support, and I'm just trying to get through this tough time. (looking up) I'm glad you asked, though. I think it's good that you're checking in with me about that. (smiling slightly) It makes me feel like you care, and that you're looking out for me.

The patient presents with persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, indicating a potential risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's emotional distress and feelings of being overwhelmed warrant close monitoring and support. It's essential to approach this situation with empathy and understanding, acknowledging the challenges of the postpartum experience.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 26, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient indicates they can laugh, but it's a 'tired laugh' and not as frequent or enjoyable as before, matching 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have not been looking forward to things as they used to, and even things they used to enjoy no longer seem appealing, with only rare exceptions like their baby's smile or quiet moments to themselves, aligning with 'Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a frequent and intense pattern of self-blame, with thoughts of inadequacy and failure as a mother, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, quite a lot' option.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>Patient explicitly states feeling sad and miserable, mentioning it's a persistent feeling, using phrases like 'I've been feeling so sad and miserable lately' and 'I'm just feeling empty and sad', indicating it's most of the time.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses indicate a potential risk for <med>postpartum depression</med> and <med>anxiety</med>, characterized by persistent <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, and difficulty coping with daily responsibilities. The EPDS score of 26 suggests a high possibility of depression, and the patient's symptoms align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's emotional distress and feelings of being overwhelmed warrant close monitoring and support. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> to improve sleep quality
3. Develop a support network, including family, friends, and support groups
4. Consider referral to a <med>lactation consultant</med> for breastfeeding support
5. Encourage self-care activities, such as exercise, meditation, or hobbies
6. Provide resources for <med>postpartum depression</med> and <med>anxiety</med>, including online support groups and hotlines
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
